stories.title: High nominal yields with ACM term‑premium evidence; long‑end decomposition still unresolved
stories.whatChanged: 10Y nominal yields remain elevated and New York Fed ACM shows a governed 10Y term premium around 0.73% (declining modestly over five sessions).
stories.whyItMatters: A nontrivial nominal yield and observed term premium raise financing costs and make credit sensitive to further yield moves; decomposition into real vs breakeven vs residual matters for policy/credit transmission.
stories.mechanism: Higher real yields and persistent nominal yields lift borrowing costs; if credit and volatility follow, equity breadth could narrow beyond megacaps.
stories.conclusion: Governed term‑premium evidence is present and nominal yields remain high, but the long‑end decomposition (real vs breakeven vs residual) and volatility confirmation are unresolved and block attribution of yield moves to supply, inflation or term‑premium.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: A canonical MOVE/Treasury‑volatility series and consistent real/breakeven intraday observations that show coordinated directional moves would permit a clear decomposition.

stories.title: High‑yield spreads have widened materially while IG and large‑cap breadth remain relatively intact
stories.whatChanged: HY OAS widened substantially over recent 20‑session windows while IG OAS moved modestly and large‑cap breadth stays above averages.
stories.whyItMatters: Selective HY stress can precede broader credit deterioration if sustained; if contained, it signals idiosyncratic or sectoral stress rather than systemic market dislocation.
stories.mechanism: Issuer/sector concentration or duration/sensitivity differences lift HY spreads faster than IG; sustained yield pressure could broaden the move into IG and equity breadth.
stories.conclusion: HY widening is a real signal of stress in riskier credit buckets, but IG spreads and large‑cap breadth do not yet confirm a broad market stress.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Sustained coordinated IG widening, a canonical MOVE rise and persistent breadth deterioration beyond megacaps would change this assessment.

stories.title: Meta Q3 beat and stronger guidance sustain AI/megacap leadership, transmission to rates unresolved
stories.whatChanged: Canonical coverage and SEC XBRL filings report a revenue beat and stronger guidance; Meta cites new AI model milestones and higher capex guidance context.
stories.whyItMatters: If megacap guidance lifts risk appetite, it could push short‑term rates and futures; absence of intraday market timestamps prevents confirming immediate macro transmission.
stories.mechanism: Stronger guidance can re‑ignite risk‑on flows into megacaps; without intraday futures/FX/gold evidence, we cannot confirm same‑session macro repricing.
stories.conclusion: Meta’s earnings and guidance are confirmed in canonical news and filings and support the AI/megacap leadership narrative; whether that lifted rates or safe havens in the same session is unresolved.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Timestamped Fed‑funds‑futures and 2Y/10Y intraday bars plus DXY/XAUUSD around the release showing appreciable moves would confirm transmission.

verified.detail: Nvidia and Apple together accounted for more than 15% of the S&P 500, reinforcing the concentration risk behind an index that can remain firm even when participation is weaker.

verified.title: Saudi/Houthi energy risk persists
verified.detail: Saudi-led coalition forces said six Houthi ballistic missiles were intercepted on 24 September, with Yanbu among the targeted areas; the report also described claimed attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu.

verified.title: Duration stress is global
verified.detail: A Bloomberg global sovereign-bond yield gauge approached 4%, the highest level since 2007, supporting the view that duration pressure is global rather than solely a U.S. Treasury story.

verified.title: Natural-gas storage tightened
verified.detail: EIA reported Lower-48 working gas at 3,351 Bcf for the week ended 18 September 2026, a 53 Bcf weekly injection and 95 Bcf above the five-year average.

verified.title: NBIS analyst catalyst verified
verified.detail: BNP Paribas upgraded Nebius Group from Neutral to Outperform and raised its price target from $260 to $399 on 24 September 2026, independently confirming a catalyst cited in the StockedUp transcript.

verified.title: US–China tariff cliff pushed out
verified.detail: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. and China agreed to extend their trade truce through 10 January 2027, reducing the immediate tariff-cliff risk while broader negotiations continue.

verified.title: US–Iran diplomacy is active
verified.detail: President Trump said U.S.-Iran talks were continuing during the UN General Assembly and that he believed a settlement would be reached; this verifies active diplomacy but not the transcript's specific Hormuz-for-sanctions terms.

verified.title: Diesel export-policy risk
verified.detail: The U.S. Chamber warned that restricting U.S. diesel or fuel exports could squeeze refiners and risk reducing supplies of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel, potentially worsening consumer costs.

verified.title: Late-September midterm seasonality
verified.detail: Citadel Securities' historical midterm-year path shows equities tending to weaken into around September 30 before a stronger average year-end phase; this supports late-September seasonality as context, not a forecast.

verified.title: META Muse catalyst verified
verified.detail: Meta launched its Muse personal AI agent and said it planned integration with smart glasses, independently confirming the product catalyst behind the creator's META discussion.

verified.title: RKLB defence-space catalyst verified
verified.detail: Rocket Lab said it was selected for the U.S. Space Force NITE-STAR IDIQ program, which has a ceiling of up to $981 million across participating vendors, confirming the defence-space catalyst cited by StockedUp.
